title: A chain-boundary re-exec restarts the chain's batch count and max_batches
summary: PR #712 made a wave-boundary re-exec resume the batch's wave index (a pid-keyed handoff with waves_done, taken once at boot). A chain-boundary re-exec (the chain Driver's refresh between batches) still starts the new process's chain at batch 0 with the full max_batches, so a long --until-inbox-empty chain whose batches keep landing go/ changes can run past its runaway backstop. max_batches is a backstop, not the operator budget, and the brake and inbox-empty stops still apply, so this is low severity.
fix: Carry the chain's completed-batch count across its re-exec the same way the wave handoff does: a dedicated marker field written only by the chain boundary, taken once at boot into loopConfig, honoured by the Driver's first boundary.
acceptance: A chain re-exec after k batches resumes at batch k with max_batches-k left (red today: it restarts at 0)
A wave-boundary handoff and a chain handoff never read each other's field
